ac_results.ac: D4 Quote engine: spread widens with uncertainty; skew follows inventory; complement p+q<1-margin; each pull rule fires
ac_results.command: probe.py D4 section (market_intents plus full LadderEngine.on_tick)
ac_results.evidence: As unc goes 0 to 0.08, the spread goes [0.02,0.02,0.04,0.06,0.10]. As vol goes 0, 0.02, 0.05, it goes 0.02, 0.04, 0.06. At engine level, a larger sigma_rel_unc gives a wider spread. Skew: long YES lowers the YES bid and long NO lowers the NO bid at net 10/30/45. Complement: 3000 random holdings >= min_size with random costs and mids gave 3000 complement bids, all with cost + bid < 0.99 and size <= held. Pulls fire on their triggers and the engine emits nothing: close at E-10min and E-1ms; the oracle gap at E, E+1min and E+1h; a book 60,001 ms old; a feed 5,001 ms old. There is no pull at exactly 60,000 / 5,000 ms. A sharp move at 1.05x the independently computed threshold (11.26 bp) pulls and 0.95x does not; a move spread over 20 s (longer than the window) does not. A crossed book pulls with a data_fault record. A reference tick moves the quotes (requote). Minor gap: complement bids apply only to holdings >= min_size (see defects).

defects.description: Complement-bid price cap is skipped for holdings below min_size. quotes() applies the p+q<1-margin cap only when held_other >= m.min_size. With a smaller holding (for example a partial maker fill of 3-4.99 shares), the bid on the other outcome is a plain quote with no cap. Reproduced: holding 4 YES at 0.60 with the mid now 0.40, the engine posts a NO bid at 0.59 x 10, so a fill pairs 4 shares at p+q = 1.19 against 1-margin = 0.99. That locks a loss on merge and contradicts the requirement 'holding one outcome bought at p, bid the other at q with p + q < 1 - margin'. The loss is bounded below min_size shares, and paper only.
defects.fix_hint: In quotes(), when 0 < held_other < min_size and the cost is known, still cap px at 1 - cost[other] - margin (strictly below), keeping the plain size. If the cost is unknown, skip the bid, as the complement path does. Add one test case with a 4-share holding.

defects.description: Role 23's invariant is checked only on the YES-side (f, m, q). NO-side intents carry 1-f, 1-mid, 1-q, which under float rounding can break sign/magnitude when |f-mid| <= 4.4e-16. A probe with f within 2 ulps of mid emitted 2717 intents whose parsed reason fails invariant_ok. With real data this can't practically happen (f comes from a CDF, mid is on the tick grid), but the downstream invariant suite would count it as a violation.
defects.fix_hint: In market_intents, run invariant_ok on the exact (ff, mm, qq) written into each intent's reason before emitting it, or compute the NO q as shrink(1-f, 1-mid).

Verdict PASS: all of D1-D7 are code-level and verified independently with auditor probes, not only the builder's tests. There are no [ops] criteria in WP1-D. Two minor defects (above) do not block. Observations for WP1-F:
(a) The selector ranks purely on income per dollar, so a market holding inventory could in principle fall outside max_markets and lose its complement or skewed quotes. My probe could not reproduce this: a cheap complement bid raises that market's income. It is a design note, not a defect.
(b) With a non-default pull_before_close_ms below about 5 min, expiry = end - 3 min can land under now + 2 min. The kernel's GTD rule would reject it, so it fails closed. The defaults are safe.
(c) The builder's live dry-run figures (4.6 ms per tick, 24/24 checkpoint rows live, the example quotes) were not reproduced; the scripts were in the builder's scratchpad and are not ACs. A synthetic worst case (158 markets all quotable at tau 6h, 154 strikes in one ladder, so the ladder_arbs O(n^2) scan dominates) measured 46.8 ms per on_tick. Keep this in mind if the loop calls on_tick on every Binance trade.
(d) The stale_feed check uses ref ts_ms, which WP1-C sets to Binance event time E, so local clock skew over 5 s would pull every quote (or never pull, if the skew runs the other way).
(e) WP1-F must drain engine.records, call on_fill (and replay it on restart), trip role 02 on data_fault records, and have the human confirm PREREG before it is written, as the builder listed.
